messages:
sara: Hey team — ACME Private customer reporting intermittent streaming failures from our private inference endpoint. They say requests sometimes start fine but streaming chunks drop after ~10-30s with TLS errors. They rolled a firewall change right before seeing this.
jamal: Can you paste the client curl + any TLS errors or server-side logs you have? Also what did they change on the firewall (SG / NACL / proxy)?
sara: Repro steps they gave:
```curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" https://acme-private.api:443/v1/streams?model=redwood-13b
# response 200, stream begins, then connection closes after ~20s with no more chunks
```
Client-side error: `tls: unexpected message` then `read tcp 10.0.2.5:47122->54.211.32.10:443: read: connection reset by peer`
Server logs: a couple of `stream write failed: write tcp 172.16.5.12:443->100.64.1.23:32005: write: connection reset by peer` entries around same time.
mike: That pattern usually points at NAT/ephemeral port restrictions or a middlebox doing TLS inspect and resetting sessions. Do they have narrowed ephemeral port ranges or a strict egress allowlist? NACLs are stateless so they can easily break return traffic.
sara: They said they tightened outbound NACLs to only allow source ports 1024-1025 (they thought restricting source ephemeral ports for security was fine). Also they set DNS egress to only 10.0.0.53:53.
jamal: Oof — restricting source ports like that will break TCP flows. TCP return packets from remote IPs/SYN-ACKs are matched against ephemeral source ports on NAT addresses; if the NAT chooses a port outside their tiny allowed range, the NACL will drop the response. For streaming connections with keepalives, port churn is expected. Recommend they allow a full ephemeral range. Also confirm there isn't an inline TLS proxy rewriting records (that can show `unexpected message`).
sara: Customer ran tcpdump on their NAT: `tcpdump -n "host 54.211.32.10 and port 443"` and saw SYN, SYN-ACK, then RST after ~20s. SNAT uses 100.64.x.x with source ports in 32000-32010. Their NACL only permitted 1024-1025, so RSTs likely dropped.
deploy-bot: Note: outbound NACL rule change (id: rule-88) applied to acme-private VPC at 2024-11-08T15:12Z.
mike: Actionable support response: 1) Ask customer to widen outbound ephemeral range to at least 1024-32767 (recommended 1024-65535). 2) Temporarily add an outbound NACL allow 1024-65535 -> 0.0.0.0/0 and retest streaming. 3) If they use a DPI/TLS-inspecting proxy, bypass for api endpoints and retest. Example minimal NACL snippet: ```# NACL outbound allow ephemeral
Rule #: 100
Protocol: TCP
Port range: 1024-65535
Destination: 0.0.0.0/0
Action: ALLOW```
sara: Sent those steps to customer and asked them to try widening ephemeral ports and to provide a pcap if it still fails. I'll update thread when they respond. Thanks! :thumbsup:
jamal: Also remind them SGs are stateful so they don't need inbound rules for ephemeral return traffic; NACLs are the usual culprit.
sara: noted, closing for now pending customer retest.
